$comment: Canonical shared CONFIGURATION. Everything about the vehicle's shape that is NOT a design variable but that more than one discipline needs to agree on. Every publication must reference this by id+version+hash, exactly as it references the design space. Two publications with different configuration_ref describe different aircraft and must not be intersected.
description: Shared geometric and material assumptions for the uav-medium design space. These were previously duplicated across aero/geometry.py, structures/beam.py, weights/mass.py and the dashboard, with no mechanism to detect disagreement -- and they did disagree.

planform.$comment: The dashboard silhouettes used taper 0.45 against the AVL decks' 0.50. Neither was wrong on its own; nothing could see that they differed.

tail.$comment: Horizontal tail sized by volume coefficient. The ARM is the load-bearing number here: it sets how long the fuselage has to be, which is a weights quantity derived from an aero assumption. That was the undeclared interface.

fuselage.$comment: length_rule is the fix for the interface above. Sizing on volume alone produced a body 2.9-5.0 m too short to mount the empennage, and roughly 43 kg of skin that nobody was paying for.

materials.$comment: The round-6 campaign event switches spar_caps to carbon_uni. Changing a material here changes the configuration hash, which is exactly right: it invalidates every publication that was derived under the old one.

lattice.$comment: Vortex-lattice density for the AVL decks. Kept here because structures reads the spanload from the same solve and must not silently use a different discretisation.
